newsitem.title: USA: Kansas row crop conditions improve in week.
newsitem.headline: Kansas row crop conditions improve in week.

text.p: The following is the weekly crop summary from the Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service for the week ending August 17.

Row crop conditions and soil moisture supplies improved, according to Kansas Agricultural Statistics and the Kansas State University Extension Service. Cooler temperatures and scattered rains have allowed crop progress to continue ahead of average.

Corn condition is reported as 12 percent excellent, 57 percent good, 25 percent fair, 5 percent poor, and 1 percent very poor(see table 1). Currently, 75 percent of the corn is in the dough stage. This compares to 87 percent last year and the average of 67 percent. Twenty-eight percent of the crop is dented, behind 1996 at 47 percent but slightly ahead of the 27 percent average. Sorghum condition is reported as 12 percent excellent, 64 percent good, 20 percent fair, and 4 percent poor. Sorghum headed is 88 percent complete, behind 1996 at 90 percent but ahead of the five-year average of 64 percent. Fifteen percent of the sorghum crop is coloring, compared to 14 percent in 1996 and the average of 9 percent. Soybean condition is 8 percent excellent, 62 percent good, 28 percent fair, and 2 percent poor. Ninety-nine percent of the soybean crop is blooming, ahead of both 1996 at 95 percent and the average of 89 percent. Statewide, 87 percent of the crop is setting pods, compared to 72 percent in 1996 and 63 percent for the average. Only a small percentage of the soybean crop has begun to drop their leaves. Condition of the sunflower crop is 8 percent excellent, 62 percent good, 19 percent fair, 8 percent poor, and 3 percent very poor. Statewide, eighty-five percent of the sunflower crop has begun to petal and forty-six percent is blooming. In the northwest district, 83 percent of the crop has begun to petal and 36 percent of the crop is blooming.
Third cutting of alfalfa is 80 percent complete, compared to last year at 90 percent and 79 percent for the five-year average. Fourth cutting is 18 percent complete.

Statewide, there were 3.3 days suitable for fieldwork during the week (see table 3). The major field activities this week were fertilizing, managing irrigation equipment, working wheat stubble, and cutting alfalfa. Topsoil moisture is rated 3 percent very short, 19 percent short, 69 percent adequate, and 9 percent surplus. Subsoil moisture is rated 4 percent very short, 23 percent short, 71 percent adequate, and 2 percent surplus.

Pasture condition for the State is rated 10 percent excellent, 47 percent good, 32 percent fair, 7 percent poor, and 4 percent very poor. Cattle are continuing to move off of grass. Stock water supplies remain mostly adequate.
